offered_action_specs.name: rollback_deploy
offered_action_specs.description: Roll one service back to the settings it ran before its latest deploy, as the deploy log records them. Its container is recreated, so the service pauses while it restarts. Money already booked wrong stays wrong: a rollback stops new damage, and repairs nothing.

proposed.why: The deploy log and the receiver's metrics agree: since the v2 secret deploy every webhook is rejected as bad_signature and none is queued, so the provider keeps retrying and our books cannot catch up.

diagnosis.hypothesis: At 07:59:04 webhook-receiver was redeployed with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2. The provider still signs its webhooks with the previous secret, so the receiver now fails the signature check on every webhook. It replies with a rejection instead of an acknowledgement and never puts the event on provider-events. The provider retries each unacknowledged webhook, and each retry is rejected again. So the received rate climbs, nothing reaches ledger-consumer or payment-confirmer, and the money check cannot settle: 131 webhooks were unacknowledged at the last evaluation. The evidence does not show which secret version the provider uses, or whether the v2 secret is wrong or just not yet rotated on the provider's side. Either way, the receiver and the provider now disagree on the secret. The receiver logged nothing at WARN or ERROR for these rejections, so they show only in the metric.

evidence.shows: webhook-receiver was recreated at 07:59:04Z with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2, the latest deploy, about a minute before the alert at 07:59:52Z. The other services were last deployed at 07:57:38Z.

Before the deploy all webhooks were result=queued (about 3.9/s at 07:59:01). From 07:59:21 result=bad_signature appears and grows to 19.3/s by 08:00:21, while queued falls to 0.9/s and then stops reporting. Every webhook is now rejected.
The total webhook rate rose from about 4/s to 18.8/s after the deploy, which fits the provider retrying rejected, unacknowledged webhooks.
The receiver logged no WARN or ERROR lines in the last 10 minutes, so the signature rejections are not logged at those levels.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll webhook-receiver back to its settings before the 07:59:04 deploy, so it uses the previous webhook secret version the provider still signs with. The provider's retries should then be accepted and queued, and the consumers can catch up. Afterwards, check that klaxon_webhooks_received_total{result="bad_signature"} drops to zero, then run money_check. Re-attempt the v2 rotation only once the provider signs with v2, or once the receiver accepts both versions.

diagnosis.blast_radius: webhook-receiver pauses while its container is recreated. The provider keeps retrying meanwhile, so no webhooks should be lost. After the rollback a burst of retried webhooks will be queued, and the consumers face a short spike in load and lag. Duplicate deliveries are possible, but the consumers run idempotent and by_our_id handlers. If the v2 rotation was needed for security, rolling back keeps the old secret in use for longer.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the rollback makes things worse, redeploy webhook-receiver with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2. Make sure the provider signs with v2 first, or the same rejections will return.
